entry.title: Mrs Karen Brown v St John of God [2026] FWC 3894
entry.content:
Karen Brown lodged an unfair dismissal application under s 394 of the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) after her dismissal on 29 July 2026, but the application was lodged on 22 August 2026, outside the 21-day period. The Fair Work Commission considered whether to extend time, found no exceptional circumstances, and dismissed the application. The case is a straightforward extension-of-time decision.

Key holding: An unfair dismissal application lodged out of time can only proceed if the Commission is satisfied that exceptional circumstances exist, assessed by the s 394(3) factors.

The Commission can only extend time if it is satisfied that there are 'exceptional circumstances', taking into account the matters in ss 394(3)(a) to (f).

entry.title: Ms Genevieve Dwyer v The Australian Broadcasting Corporation [2026] FWC 2762
entry.content:
Genevieve Dwyer applied under s739 of the Fair Work Act to resolve a dispute with the ABC about the interpretation of cl 54.6.3 of the ABC Enterprise Agreement 2022-2025. She argued that being on approved personal leave without pay at the time of a redundancy notification brought her within cl 54.6.3 (which allows employees on annual leave, long service leave or leave without pay to complete that leave).

Fair Work Commission, 22 Jul 2026, [2026] FWC 2762

entry.title: Ms Amanda Ferrari v Virbac (Australia) Pty Ltd & Nikki Cuff [2026] FWC 2527
entry.content:
Ms Ferrari lodged a general protections dismissal application 5 weeks and 6 days late, alleging dismissal shortly after disclosing a disability. The Commission found no exceptional circumstances, noting ignorance of the 21-day time limit is not exceptional and the merits were arguable but not strong. The application was dismissed.

Fair Work Commission, 3 Jul 2026, [2026] FWC 2527

entry.title: Dr Jennifer Weber v Caroline Chisholm Society [2026] FWC 331
entry.content:
Dr Jennifer Weber, former CEO of Caroline Chisholm Society, applied for an unfair dismissal remedy after her employment ended on 14 February 2025. The employer objected that she was excluded from protection because her earnings exceeded the high income threshold of $175,000. Deputy President Bell found that although her earnings (including the private use value of her vehicle) exceeded the threshold, she was covered by the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award 2020, so the jurisdictional objection was dismissed.

Fair Work Commission, 5 Feb 2026, [2026] FWC 331

entry.title: Cowra Meat Processors Pty Limited v Mr Leigh Moiler [2025] FWC 2968
entry.content:
Cowra Meat Processors sought a stay of a Commissioner's order that it reinstate Mr Moiler pending its appeal against the unfair dismissal decision. VP Gibian granted the stay on conditions, requiring CMP to pay Mr Moiler his usual wages pending the November Full Bench appeal without seeking recovery, having found the appeal arguable but the balance finely balanced.

Fair Work Commission, 3 Oct 2025, [2025] FWC 2968

entry.title: Mrs Jia Ye v Marubeni Australia Ltd [2025] FWC 2368
entry.content:
The applicant filed a general protections application alleging adverse action based on race, sex, and pregnancy. The employer objected, arguing that a prior discrimination complaint under NSW law barred the application under s732. The Commission found that the discrimination complaint was made before the dismissal and thus was not 'in relation to the dismissal' as required by s732, so the application could proceed.

Fair Work Commission, 13 Aug 2025, [2025] FWC 2368

entry.title: Mr Yi-Hsien Chou v Steadfast Shareholding Pty Ltd [2025] FWC 1617
entry.content:
The employer applied to indefinitely adjourn an unfair dismissal proceeding pending civil proceedings in the District Court of Queensland. Deputy President Butler dismissed the stay application, distinguishing Teys and finding the employer's material insufficient to deprive the applicant of his right to have the unfair dismissal application determined. The substantive question of whether the dismissal was harsh, unjust and unreasonable remains reserved.

Fair Work Commission, 13 Jun 2025, [2025] FWC 1617
